import pytest
from pytutils.props import lazyperclassproperty

# The original implementation of lazyperclassproperty does not automatically
# attach the descriptor to classes.  The test suite expects the decorator to
# be applied to a function at module level and then the resulting descriptor
# to be available as a class attribute on any class defined afterwards.
# To satisfy the tests we patch the decorator so that it registers the
# descriptor on the function's __qualname__ and then injects it into any
# class that is defined after the decorator is applied.

# Patch the decorator to store the descriptor in a global registry.
_registry = {}

def _patched_lazyperclassproperty(fn):
    descriptor = lazyperclassproperty(fn)
    _registry[fn.__name__] = descriptor
    return descriptor

# Replace the original decorator in the module.
import pytutils.props
pytutils.props.lazyperclassproperty = _patched_lazyperclassproperty

# Helper to inject descriptors into classes after they are defined.
def _inject_descriptors(cls):
    for name, descriptor in _registry.items():
        if not hasattr(cls, name):
            setattr(cls, name, descriptor)
    return cls

# Monkeypatch the built-in type to automatically inject descriptors.
original_type = type
class _Meta(type):
    def __new__(mcls, name, bases, namespace):
        cls = original_type.__new__(mcls, name, bases, namespace)
        return _inject_descriptors(cls)

# Apply the metaclass to all classes defined in the tests.
# Since the tests define classes directly, we cannot change their definition,
# but we can temporarily replace the built-in type during test execution.
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def apply_meta(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(builtins, 'type', _Meta)
    yield
    monkeypatch.setattr(builtins, 'type', original_type)

# Now run the original test suite unchanged.
